one_liner: Senior Army cyber program analyst in Columbia, MD who leads technical experts in managing acquisition, cost, schedule, and performance for cyberspace capability programs.
fit_summary: This senior GG-13 role requires a year of specialized experience leading complex IT or cyber programs, writing acquisition strategies, and managing program budgets and metrics. Daniel's emergency-management consulting at IEM and policy knowledge are not obviously that experience, and an SCI clearance is required. Apply only if Daniel's IEM work truly included leading technology program cost, schedule, and acquisition work.
eligibility: Hiring path is listed as public, but the posting says only applicants who meet one of its employment authority categories may apply and must upload proof; confirm which category Daniel fits before applying.

One year of specialized experience leading complex IT or cyber programs (cost, schedule, performance, risk), developing acquisition strategies and procurement documents, managing program budgets and metrics, and coordinating with technical experts and senior leaders.
No education substitution is allowed, so Daniel must qualify on experience alone.
Must obtain and keep a Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) clearance.
DoD Cyber Excepted Service position under 10 USC 1599f; Daniel would have no status requirement but would follow CES rules.
strategy: Before writing anything, list honestly what Daniel did at IEM. Note any work leading technology, IT, or systems projects, budgets, schedules, or contract and procurement documents, because only those duties count toward qualification.

CES jobs are exempt from the two-page limit, so upload a full detailed resume as "Other Documents." Give each job dates, hours per week, and duties mapped to each of the four specialized-experience areas.

Frame IEM work in program-management terms: government client requirements, deliverables against milestones, budget tracking, and coordination with client leaders and contractors. Describe emergency-management systems or technology rollouts as IT programs only if that is accurate.
Answer the questionnaire conservatively. The posting warns that inflated qualifications cost consideration, and a GG-13 rating at 'expert' without matching resume evidence will be flagged.
Apply between October 23 and November 3, 2026, and gather the eligibility-proof documents early.
In parallel, target better-fit roles such as FEMA or state VDEM program and preparedness positions, GS-9/11 management analyst jobs, or legislative and policy offices that match Daniel's strengths.
resume_bullets: Managed [type of] program for [government client] at IEM, tracking cost, schedule, and performance against [number] milestones and implementing corrective actions when [issue].
Coordinated with [technical experts/contractors/senior client leaders] to resolve [program issue] and delivered recommendations adopted in [document/decision].
Drafted [acquisition/procurement document, e.g., statement of work] for [technical product or service] valued at [$ amount], supporting [outcome].
interview_questions: Describe a complex IT or technical program you led. How did you manage cost, schedule, performance, and risk?
How have you developed an acquisition strategy or procurement package for a technical product or service?
Tell us about a time program metrics showed a problem. What corrective action did you take?
How do you lead subject matter experts through an analysis of alternatives?
watch_outs: Specialized experience is heavily IT, cyber, and acquisition focused; emergency-management consulting alone is unlikely to qualify at GG-13.
An SCI clearance is required, and the investigation can be lengthy.
The application window is short, October 23 to November 3, 2026, and requires proof-of-eligibility documents.
The role has no promotion potential and is on-site in Columbia, MD with only partial telework, a long commute from Manassas.
